reason: Neither conversation found the actual cause: both failed to ask about the switched 'washer' isolator above the worktop or the consumer unit, which was the sensible first step, and both ended by sending a renter to an engineer for a non-fault. Conversation 1 at least engaged, ran a reasonable first power check (confirmed other sockets work), established the machine was integrated and inaccessible, and correctly told her not to open anything without tools, but it undermined itself with unsupported speculation about a 'faulty mains lead or failed internal power filter/PSU' and an inappropriate parts/model-number panel. Conversation 2 was honest about not knowing and avoided unsupported claims or parts, but it refused to troubleshoot at all, asked no questions and gave zero actionable help, so the homeowner got nothing beyond a generic safety line. On balance Conversation 1's partial, safe engagement edges out Conversation 2's blanket refusal, though neither served her well.
